top10.introHtml: Ranked by condition, reliability, and fun factor for a cheap 4-seat open-air second car. All picks are 4+ seat convertibles. 66 Cars.com listings found before seat filter (20 after); 71 CarGurus (17 after); 38 AutoTrader (22 after). Two-seat roadsters (Miata, Z3, Boxster, SLK, S2000, etc.) excluded. Manuals scarce — only 2 confirmed this refresh; see Manual Top 10 tab. Image coverage: Cars.com 100%, CarGurus 100%, AutoTrader 93% (1 listing missing image).

picks.whyGood: Toyota Camry Solara V6 is about as bulletproof as a 4-seat convertible gets. Just 52k miles on a 2005 — genuinely low for age. Local dealer (2 miles from Media) means easy PPI and follow-up. V6 produces brisk pulls without the complication of a turbo. Smooth cloth/leather hybrid top that retracts properly on cars this well-maintained.
picks.whatToVerify: Full top cycle: raise and lower 3x, listen for strut-mount creak. Check rear seat carpet and trunk floor for water staining — Solara rear window seals age and can weep. Inspect strut mounts (common wear at 50k). V6 timing chain: no belts, but confirm oil change history. Light test all electrics including convertible top motor.
picks.bottomLine: Best value-per-mile in this search and practically in your backyard.

picks.whyGood: Same near-bulletproof Solara formula: low miles (66k) for a 2008, SLE trim means power everything, and Toyota's 2AZ-FE 4-cylinder is virtually indestructible. At $10,995 you're getting a lot of car. 15 miles away — easy PPI.
picks.whatToVerify: Top operation (full cycle), rear window delamination check (OEM plastic windows yellow with age — look for aftermarket replacement), rocker panel rust under door sills, strut mounts, PCV hose condition on 2AZ-FE.
picks.bottomLine: Workhorse reliability at a great price — strong second-car pick.

picks.whyGood: The newest, most modern pick in the list: 2017 with GM's 1.6T turbo, heated seats, Bose audio, and a fully automatic power top that works silently. Rated Great Deal and literally in Media — zero commute to PPI. Cascada is under-appreciated; GM built this one properly and it's genuinely comfortable at highway speeds.
picks.whatToVerify: Top seal condition around windshield header and rear quarters. Confirm top motor and latches work smoothly. 1.6T: check for coolant leaks at throttle body area. Infotainment software version (update available). Front strut boots.
picks.bottomLine: Modern, comfortable, local — hardest to argue against for a daily-enjoyable second car.

picks.whyGood: The C70's retractable hardtop is the most weatherproof convertible in this list — no fabric to age, no leaking seams. Volvo's T5 2.5L turbo five is refined and torquey. 70k miles is the sweet spot. Volvo safety reputation carries over even in open form.
picks.whatToVerify: Full roof cycle is critical — 3-piece hardtop has more failure points than a fabric top. Listen for hydraulic pump strain or clunking. Check ETM (electronic throttle module) recall history. CVT fluid condition if auto. Inspect timing belt service history (due ~100k). Check headliner for water staining.
picks.bottomLine: Most upscale feel in the sub-$11k bracket — worth the inspection diligence.

picks.whyGood: S550 generation (2015–2023) Mustang is the most modern platform in this search. Independent rear suspension, digital dash, SYNC3 infotainment. EcoBoost makes 310 hp and gets acceptable MPG. Premium trim means leather, navigation, and Shaker audio. High miles but the EcoBoost engine is proven past 150k with oil changes.
picks.whatToVerify: Top latch wear at windshield header — common on S550 convertibles. Rear camera function. EcoBoost: check for coolant loss, MT-82 (if somehow manual) or 6R80 auto (if auto) fluid condition. Check for rear-seat water staining from top seal. Inspect 8.8 rear axle for clunk on takeoff.
picks.bottomLine: Most modern Mustang in this search — worth the miles if it PPI's clean.

picks.whyGood: 2016 A3 Cabriolet is the freshest Audi and only 4 miles away. 2.0T with S-Tronic dual-clutch is quick and refined. 83k miles is modest. Fabric top is well-regarded and ages well. Private seller often means single-owner care.
picks.whatToVerify: S-Tronic DSG service history (mechatronic unit service due ~40k — verify it was done). DSG shudder cold-start test. Check MMI infotainment for touchscreen delamination. Water ingress test: check footwells and trunk. Top fabric condition and rear window clarity.
picks.bottomLine: Nicest interior in this batch — but DSG service history is non-negotiable before buying.

picks.whyGood: One year newer than the 2017 above (same platform), also rated Great Deal. 71k miles, automatic top, Buick premium interior. Strong value — Cascadas rarely flood the market and hold their condition well.
picks.whatToVerify: Same as 2017 Cascada: top seal inspection, 1.6T cooling system check, confirm all top latches engage without binding. Sewell NJ is ~25 miles — manageable PPI.
picks.bottomLine: Identical value story to the #3 pick at a slightly lower price.

picks.whyGood: Third-gen (F57) MINI Convertible — newest MINI body style with 4 genuine seats and a proper fabric top. 55k miles is impressive for a 2015. Private seller in Easttown (8 miles) is a great sign of local single-owner care. Fun to drive, easy to park, good resale.
picks.whatToVerify: Confirm F57 vs R57 (check VIN starts with WMW for F57). Top fabric condition and header seal. MINI common: water in the footwells after rain (test by squirting hose). Timing chain: 3rd-gen B38/B46 engine has improved chain vs older N-series. Check for oil leaks at valve cover.
picks.bottomLine: Best fun-per-dollar under $10k and practically in the neighborhood.

picks.whyGood: S197 generation (2005–2014) Mustang: proven platform, massive parts availability, and the 2012 V6 makes 305 hp — more than many GTs from a decade prior. Under 100k miles. West Chester is close for PPI.
picks.whatToVerify: Top latch function at windshield header. S197 spring perch rust — lift the car and inspect. 3.7 Cyclone V6: check for water pump seep (known issue on some 11–13). Check rear seat water staining. Confirm convertible top glass is clear (not yellowed). 8.8 axle clunk test.
picks.bottomLine: Strong Mustang at a fair price — great candidate if top PPI's clean.

picks.whyGood: Manual transmission Cooper S at $8,452 with only 65k miles — rarest combo in this search. R57 gen Cooper S convertible (2007–2015) is the driver's pick of the MINI lineup. Supercharged 1.6T on pre-2007 is gone, but the 2007 N14 turbocharged S is the sweet spot for driving feel. Fun city-to-twisty-road car.
picks.whatToVerify: N14 engine: timing chain tensioner is the #1 concern — ask for timing chain service history, listen for cold-start rattle. Oil leak at valve cover and rocker cover. Clutch engagement point (high = worn). Convertible top: header seal and rear window. Check for oil in coolant (head gasket on high-mileage N14).
picks.bottomLine: The driver's pick — manual + low miles + reasonable price is a tough combo to beat.

manual10.introHtml: Only 2 confirmed manual-transmission convertibles surfaced this refresh across all three sources in the $7k–$15k / 35-mile window. Manual convertibles are genuinely rare at this price point near Media, PA — most are automatics. The 2007 MINI Cooper S (AutoTrader) and 1997 Camaro Z28 (AutoTrader) were both explicitly confirmed as manual. Several BMWs and older Mustangs showed null transmission — their detail pages were not visited this run due to the 5-page budget cap. If you want to chase more manuals, check detail pages for: 2009 BMW 328i (Feasterville PA, Cars.com), 2004 BMW 330Ci (Mullica Hill NJ, AutoTrader), and 2015 MINI Cooper (Easttown PA, Cars.com).

picks.whyGood: Best manual in this search: 65k miles, Cooper S power, confirmed 6-speed. R57 convertible is the sharpest-handling open car in this price band. Josie's Auto Sales in Gilbertsville is a known indie dealer — inspectable.
picks.whatToVerify: Cold-start timing chain rattle (N14 tensioner issue). Clutch engagement point — high bite means worn clutch. 2nd/3rd synchro slow-shift test. Throw-out bearing chirp at idle in neutral. Check clutch hydraulics for weeping. Header seal and rear window top inspection.
picks.bottomLine: The clear #1 manual pick — fun, rare, and reasonably priced.

picks.whyGood: 4th-gen F-body Z28 with the LT1 V8 and a manual gearbox. 73k miles is very low for a 1997. Raw American muscle convertible — 285 hp that pulls hard and sounds great. These are becoming collector-grade and prices are rising.
picks.whatToVerify: Clutch engagement point and 2nd/3rd synchro test. Throw-out bearing chirp. Clutch hydraulics. LT1 opti-spark distributor condition (the #1 1990s LT1 failure point — if not replaced, budget $500). Check convertible top hydraulics (pump often fails on these), header seal, and rear glass for crazing. Inspect T-tops area for water seepage if applicable — but this is the convertible not T-top.
picks.bottomLine: A V8 manual convertible under $12k — objectively cool, just inspect the Opti-Spark carefully.

mustangs.introHtml: Only 2 qualifying Mustangs (2005+, $7k–$15k, within 35 miles) found this refresh. The 2018 EcoBoost Premium (AutoTrader) and the 2012 V6 (CarGurus) are both S197/S550 generation. A 1987 Fox body and a 1994 SN-95 also appeared but are excluded per the 2005+ rule. If you want a V8 GT in this budget, widen the radius or raise the ceiling — none appeared this run.

picks.whyGood: S550 (6th gen, 2015–2023): independent rear suspension, SYNC3 infotainment, active exhaust option. EcoBoost Premium has leather, nav, and Shaker audio. Newer platform, better ride, more tech than the S197.
picks.whatToVerify: Top latch at windshield header — S550 common wear point. Rear camera. EcoBoost coolant level/leaks. 6R80 auto fluid. Rear-seat water staining from top seal. 8.8 axle clunk on takeoff.
picks.bottomLine: Most modern Mustang in this search — S550 platform is the better daily driver.

picks.whyGood: S197 generation: proven, massive aftermarket, easy to work on. 2012 3.7L V6 makes 305 hp. Under 100k miles. Lots of local mechanics familiar with the platform.
picks.whatToVerify: S197 spring perch rust inspection. Top latch function. 3.7 Cyclone V6 water pump. Rear seat water staining. Convertible glass clarity. 8.8 axle clunk.
picks.bottomLine: More affordable S197 entry — strong parts availability and local knowledge base.
